assessment.scope: Two-round fresh-context independent full-chapter B14 reader review across all 34 canonical paragraphs in 12 / 10 / 12 section order, section headings, annotations, caveats, and cross-chapter bridges, with complete independent answers to five comprehension and transfer questions.
assessment.findings: Resolved chronological ordering of 2002 ADP split -> 2011 ILCD -> 2018 EF 2.0 / EF 3.0–3.1, explicitly aligned short/baseline/precautionary scenarios with Individualist/Hierarchist/Egalitarian perspectives on first mention, anchored Surplus Cost Potential (SCP), clarified RIVM mineral-chapter reference to Vieira et al. 2016b without forward/backward chapter confusion, smoothed dual-view climate cross-referencing, and synchronized Note 33 closing synthesis across land, fossil and mineral examples while preserving frozen Note 1 historical scope.
answers: ILCD 2011 rejected inherent-property exergy because unit exergy does not change even when extracting the last tonne; EF later separated energy carriers on a full-substitution premise (1 MJ/MJ LHV), and even across five fossil fuels EF MJ and ReCiPe kg oil-eq correspond only conditionally after aligning LHV vs HHV and 2-decimal rounding.

EF places uranium in Resource use, fossils (1 MJ/MJ) because the ILCD flow list records uranium as an MJ energy resource and excludes it from minerals/metals, whereas Van Oers 2020 and ReCiPe 2016 keep uranium in kg elemental/mineral scarcity (citing non-energy uses and ore grade-tonnage), shifting nuclear-vs-coal resource burdens across categories.

For equal 1 kg oil-eq midpoint inputs (1 kg crude oil, ~1.190 Nm3 gas, ~2.381 kg hard coal), Table 13.2 endpoint SCP yields 0.457, ~0.358 and ~0.081 USD2013 (~5.6x oil/coal ratio; ~0.360 and ~0.0815 unrounded) because endpoint switches from combustion heat to fuel-specific reserve and cumulative cost-tonnage curves.

Brown coal and peat (~4.545 kg per 1 kg oil-eq) are blank in I/H due to missing cost/production data (unmodeled, not zero cost) and in E copy hard coal 0.034 USD2013 per kg mass without HHV scaling, giving ~0.155 USD2013 (~1.9x equal-energy hard coal) purely from the per-mass proxy.

Applying crude oil 0.457 USD2013 per kg oil-eq as a constant midpoint-to-endpoint factor would impute 0.42 * 0.457 ≈ 0.192 USD2013/kg (or 19.1/45.8 * 0.457 ≈ 0.191 USD2013/kg) to hard coal — ~5.6x the published 0.034 USD2013/kg — falsely imposing crude oil extraction cost escalation onto coal.
assessment.limits: Supports this B14 comparative unit only; broader Part IV ozone, radiation, photochemical precursor overlap, index.mdx:18 ordinary link label cleanup, Part IV continuous reread, and Programme #9 global gates remain open.
